28774.description:
Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea is one of PNG’s largest food companies, manufacturing and distributing high-quality Flour, Stock Feed, Rice, Snacks, and Bakery products throughout the country. Well-known products and brands include Flame Flour, Flame Stockfeed, Flame Oil & Sugar, Flame Rice, Bilas Bread, Skel Rice, Twisties snacks, Arthur’s Pie, and the Meadow Lea range.


At GFI, we care about making everyday food better for everyone.


Our goal is to be the leading and most innovative local food company with a mission to meet our customers’ needs for superior quality foods with brands that are trusted by families everywhere.  We are the go-to source of consumer, shopper, and customer insights to help our customer and business partners succeed.


We currently have an immediate vacancy for a 
Powerhouse Technician
 to join our already strong and vibrant engineering team in 
Lae. 
Reporting to the Utilities Manager, this role ensures the safe, efficient, and uninterrupted operation, maintenance, and repair of the plant's utility and power generation systems, including boilers, generators, air compressors, water treatment facilities, and associated equipment. The Powerhouse Technician is responsible for maintaining the reliability and performance of the powerhouse to provide continuous electricity and utility services that support manufacturing and industrial operations while ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, and operational standards.


 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




Making Safety Work and Hygiene practices as a daily HABBIT at Workplace




Always maintain Self-Hygiene, workplace Housekeeping at respective workstations


Following through and executes the Permit To Work procedure system & advising others to work Safely.


Taking part in Safety talk/walks (Lead observations) and report any safety findings (Hazard).


Ensure 100% compliance on any LOTO Procedure.




Drive “Teamwork” practice in our working environment.




Communication is very important – Provide clear, accurate & timely information/feedback to all those concerned


Attend Daily & weekly Team meetings (Toolbox, engineering work orders and others).


Attend scheduled training and organised team activities such as Stock take


Be Familiarize & be competent in allocated equipment/production process


Assist wherever applicable – have the flexibility to help others in needs & teach others




Execution of the Powerhouse generator Operation & Daily Monitoring Condition  Process
 – 
On time in Full




Execute Generator Operation tasks and provide feedback in timely manner.








Follow up on Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)






Executing PM plans as per procedure and provide findings (Spare Parts Details)






Required to monitor/Cover production lines as per overall production plans








Continuous operation of mechanical and electrical systems by performing routine inspection and maintenance, monitoring metering equipment and adjusting levels as necessary. 


Maintain system by scheduling regular inspections, cleaning, filter replacement and all other tasks necessary to keep all components performing optimally, identify and repair or replace components.


Execute Breakdown escalation process in timely manner


Responsible for collecting and providing breakdown reports to team


Take part in breakdown analysis  






 


QUALIFICATION/ EXPERIENCE




Electrical Engineering Degree/Diploma/Certificate


Minimum 3 year of experience, preferably in a manufacturing environment, with demonstrated success in a similar level position within the FMCG industries.


Previous experience in Generator operation in a manufacturing set-up


Deep understanding with Generator Operation


Possess good Genset troubleshooting skills




 


Be part of the Skel life and join a team that values healthy eating and active lifestyles and wants to share that with all the people of PNG. Email your EOI and CV/Resume in 1 PDF file and send to email: 
[email protected]
.


In the subject line address as 
"Powerhouse Technician".


Applications close 
Monday 12th October 2026.


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.








Apply

28751.description:
Inventory Lead Hand


BNG Trading Company Limited is the oldest and largest independent importer and distributor of food and consumer goods in Papua New Guinea. With a strong legacy and decades of experience, we have grown into a modern and dynamic enterprise, structured around three core business divisions. Our operations span the importation and distribution of a wide range of food and consumer products, commodity trading, and indent services.


 


BNG Trading Company Limited is seeking an 
Inventory Lead Hand
 for the Distribution Centre operations of its subsidiary, Papua Niugini Freezers, in Port Moresby. The role is responsible for maintaining accurate stock records, safeguarding stock integrity, and supporting effective inventory control. The successful candidate will lead the Inventory team’s day-to-day work and work closely with Warehouse, Dispatch, Production, QA/QC, and other departments.


 


 


Key Responsibilities




Lead and coordinate the Inventory team’s daily work, providing guidance and coaching to team members.


Process and check warehouse management system transactions so stock movements are recorded accurately and on time.


Compare physical stock with system balances; investigate discrepancies, identify root causes and follow through on corrective actions.


Conduct cycle counts, stocktakes, variance checks and stock investigations.


Maintain records of stock movements, transfers, adjustments, returns, damages and variances.


Ensure FIFO and FEFO stock rotation practices are followed and monitor short-dated, expired, damaged, blocked and quarantined stock.


Check that movements between Warehouse, Production, Dispatch and other storage locations are recorded correctly.


Prepare daily, weekly and monthly inventory reports and escalate significant discrepancies, system issues and operational concerns.


Follow company procedures and food safety and workplace health and safety requirements.


Work closely with operational teams while maintaining sound inventory controls and contributing to continuous improvement.




 


Key Qualifications & Experience




Certificate, Diploma, or Degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Warehouse Management, Business Administration, or a related field is an advantage.


Experience in inventory control, warehousing, supply chain or distribution centre operations.


Experience leading or supervising a small team.


Sound knowledge of stock control, cycle counting, stock rotation and FIFO and FEFO principles.


Experience with a warehouse management, ERP or other inventory system.


Strong attention to detail, analytical skills and the ability to investigate and resolve stock discrepancies.


Good communication skills and the ability to work with several operational departments.


Ability to meet operational deadlines and take ownership of accurate records and results.


Computer skills, including Microsoft Excel and inventory reporting.




 


If you are a hands-on team leader who values inventory accuracy and can resolve stock issues thoroughly, we encourage you to apply.


 


Apply by submitting your updated CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and suitability for the role.


Email to: 
[email protected]


Applications Deadline: 11 October 2026


 


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.


 


BNG Trading Company is an equal opportunity employer committed to workplace diversity and safety. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.








Apply

Fixed term contract up to 28 September 2028 (with possible extension)


Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea


Open to PNG national candidates only 




About Palladium


Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, and, most importantly, people's lives.
 


About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)


The PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) (SWLT) program is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its TVET sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program supports improvements in national quality assurance systems, technical college standards, graduate employability, and Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG.


The program aligns with the broader goals of the 
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, which emphasises locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth, as well as 
PNG’s Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
.


This Opportunity


As 
Communications Coordinator (Digital Content) 
you will be responsible for developing content priorities and will lead the day-to-day production of engaging multimedia content. You will work across SWLT activities, technical colleges, the Department of Higher Education, Research, Science, and Technology (DHERST) and the wider TVET sector, you will identify compelling stories and produce high-quality written, photographic and video content for digital, social media, media and public diplomacy channels.


This will include: 




Work closely with the Communications Coordinator and colleagues across SWLT to plan content, identify opportunities and support delivery of the Communications and Public Diplomacy Strategy and workplan.


Identify and develop compelling stories from across SWLT, DHERST, technical colleges and the wider TVET sector, including interviewing stakeholders and drafting media releases, social media copy, profiles, case studies and feature content.


Document SWLT activities through high-quality photography and video, including during field visits, events and program activities, and edit this material into strong digital products such as short-form videos, reels and interviews.


Develop and support social media campaigns for SWLT, DHERST and Australian Government channels, adapting content and approaches for different audiences and platforms.


Keep up to date with social media trends, platform changes and emerging content formats, and monitor performance and audience engagement to inform future content and campaigns.


Ensure all content meets agreed messaging, branding, safeguarding, consent, captioning and permissions requirements.


Maintain an organised library of photographs, video footage, interviews and other digital assets, and contribute as an active and collaborative member of the broader SWLT team.




 


Program-wide responsibilities




Understand and contribute to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required.


Adhere to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately.


Model, contribute to and support an office culture of learning and performance with colleagues, junior staff and counterparts.


This role supports and upholds the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, such as reducing resource use and promoting climate-friendly practices.


Contribute to the development and implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles
[1]
 are embedded within program delivery.




About you


You will demonstrate proven experience in the following areas:




At least five years’ relevant professional experience in journalism, digital media, multimedia storytelling, communications or content production.


A portfolio of published work demonstrating strong writing, photography and video production.


Strong interviewing, writing and editing skills, including experience producing media releases and other media-ready content.


Demonstrated professional experience in photography, videography and video editing.


Strong understanding of social media platforms, trends, campaigns and analytics.


Experience producing content in the field, including in regional or remote locations.


Ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams, while managing competing priorities and deadlines.


An understanding of the political and cultural context in PNG, with the ability to work respectfully with government counterparts and other stakeholders.


Experience working with government, donor-funded programs, education or TVET in PNG would be advantageous.




To Apply


Please submit your application online, including your CV and brief cover letter, outlining your suitability in line with the requirements of the position through

Monday 12
th
 October 2026, 11.59pm AEST

We encourage applications from all individuals and provide reasonable adjustments or accommodations where required.


Should you require any adjustments to be made due to a disability or you are a neurodivergent individual or for any other circumstance, please email our team at

This Opportunity


As 
Senior Procurement Coordinator 
you will be responsible for supporting the effective delivery of all procurement activities across the SWLT program. You will be responsible for coordinating procurement processes, maintaining procurement systems and records, supporting tendering activities, conducting supplier due diligence and ensuring compliance with Palladium and DFAT procurement requirements.


This will include: 




Support and coordinate all procurement activities in compliance with the 
Australian Commonwealth Procurement Rules (CPR’s)
, DFAT 
Value for Money
 principles, and Palladium procurement and due diligence standards.


Support the implementation of procurement plans and schedules across program activities.


Manage standard procurement processes, including requests for quotations (RFQs), market research, supplier engagement, bid receipt, and procurement documentation.


Coordinate engagement with suppliers, bidders, and other key stakeholders to ensure an efficient procurement process.


Prepare procurement documentation, including RFQs, evaluation templates, purchase requisitions, contract documentation, purchase orders and procurement summary reports.


Coordinate procurement workflow and ensure procurement activities are completed within agreed timeframes.


Support the management of competitive tender processes and evaluation activities under the direction of the Procurement Manager.


Assist with contract mobilization and assist onboarding of suppliers and contractors.


Maintain complete, accurate and auditable procurement files and records.


Ensure procurement documentation complies with Palladium, DFAT and program requirements.


Maintain procurement registers, contract registers, supplier databases and tracking systems.


Conduct supplier due diligence checks and ensure supporting documentation remains current and complete.


Monitor procurement files for quality assurance and compliance requirements.


Support procurement audit preparation and respond to requests for procurement documentation.


Assist in maintaining an approved supplier database.


Support supplier performance monitoring and documentation.


Maintain regular communication with suppliers regarding procurement requirements, contracting matters and delivery schedules.


Track contract deliverables, contract expiry dates and supplier performance issues.


Escalate supplier risks, performance concerns or compliance issues to the Procurement Manager.


Prepare regular procurement status reports, pipeline updates and procurement metrics.


Monitor procurement timelines and identify potential delays or bottlenecks.


Support expenditure tracking and procurement forecasting activities.


Provide procurement data and analysis to support management decision-making.


Assist with procurement-related reporting for internal and external stakeholders.


Contribute to the integration of social procurement principles by supporting engagement with local businesses, women-owned enterprises, youth-led businesses, people with disability, and other underrepresented groups.


Understand and contribute to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives relevant to procurement activities.


Adhere to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding policies and standards and support safe, inclusive and respectful working environments.


Uphold ethical procurement practices and immediately report conflicts of interest, integrity concerns or suspected fraud.


Support environmentally sustainable procurement practices where practical and appropriate.


Contribute to a positive, collaborative and learning-oriented team culture.


Support implementation of SWLT's six program principles: locally driven, adaptive, responsive, socially inclusive, politically informed, partnership-focused, and evidence-based delivery.




 


About you


You will demonstrate proven experience in the following areas:




Extensive procurement experience in PNG, ideally within DFAT‑funded or donor‑funded development programs


Strong understanding of the Commonwealth Procurement Rules, DFAT procurement requirements and PNG Government procurement processes.


Demonstrated capacity to manage full procurement cycles including complex tenders.


Demonstrated strong analytical thinking and proactive problem solving.


Experience working with suppliers and stakeholders across PNG, including provincial contexts.


An understanding of tertiary and vocational education and training development in the Pacific Islands context is desirable.


Excellent organisational and computer skills especially with MS Word and Excel.


Operate with high levels of integrity, consistent with the intent of 
DFAT’s Ethics, Integrity and Professional Standards Policy Manual.


Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team.


Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion.

Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Joining our APD team, you will work alongside a team of APD officers to ensure the safety of our growing gold site in the Eastern Highlands.


Key Accountabilities




Responsible for the efficient and cost-effective management of the department within the established policy and in accordance with the authority delegated by the Supervisor, Asset protection.


Have fair understanding on voluntary principles on security and human rights and anti-fraud policy.


Inspect and adjust security systems, equipment, and machinery to ensure operational use and to detect evidence of tampering.


Drive and guard vehicle to transport money and valuables to prevent theft and ensure safe delivery.


May possibly require working extended hours and sometimes being involved in circumstances that can be unsafe, because of the core duties associated with which is often to look after valuable possessions and persons.


Conducting random breathalyzer test to company employees, contractors, and visitors.


To inspect and conduct searches to avoid employees and stakeholders from entering company premises with alcohol, illegal drugs and weapons or departing with company assets.


Be involved in the clearance of terminated employees to ensure smooth exit process.


Where required, liaise with Community Relations on law-and-order issues concerning impact local communities and surroundings.


Ensure the effectiveness of emergency fire and rescue response by regular training to enhance the capability of the teams.


Arresting of illegal miners


Ensure the safety rules and other policies of the camp and mine site are observed and report any suspicious activities.


Attend to other security administrative duties in line with role and as instructed by immediate Supervisor.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.


Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.




About You 


To be considered for this role, you must have a minimum of 5 years’ experience as a trained and competent security officer as well as




Have at least 3 years or more in a mining environment but must have worked previously as police, correctional services, or military personnel or similar with no criminal record.


Possess training equivalent to Police/Correctional or Military.


PNG Drivers Licence


Strong leadership and decision-making skills.


Excellent interpersonal and negotiating skills.


Can be able to manage the safety and/or security and asset protection department.


Physically fit and healthy.


Site security experience in the extractive industries (Mining, Oil & Gas)


Possess strong influencing and negotiation skills and the ability to develop and maintain constructive relationships with management, team members, peers, police, and other external agencies


Demonstrate strong conceptual skills, and capable of developing lateral and practical solutions


Organize and interpret field data and identify necessary corrections


Prepare clear, concise, and accurate investigative and narrative reports




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

28558.description:
Team Leader – Industry and Institutions – Strongim Wok Long TVET




Fixed term contract up to November 2029


Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea


All applications must be submitted through the Palladium website or they will not be considered




About Palladium


Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.


About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)


PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government, through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program focuses on supporting the Government of PNG to strengthen the national TVET system to promote quality TVET; supporting technical colleges to deliver high-quality TVET training; enhancing the diversity and employability of TVET graduates; and elevating Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG in the TVET sector.


SWLT is the primary mechanism to support PNG and Australia to deliver on commitments made under the revised Joint Statement of Intent on TVET signed at the 2024 Australia-Papua New Guinea Ministerial Forum. It also aligns with PNG’s 
Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
, as well as broader goals articulated in the 
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, including locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth.


This Opportunity


The 
Team Leader - Industry and Institutions
 is responsible for leading and overseeing (or provides strategic and operational leadership for) SWLT engagement with higher education institutions (HEIs), industry-linked initiatives, and institutional strengthening activities. The role supports delivery against Outcomes 2, 3, and 4 of the SWLT program logic and ensures that implementation is strategically aligned, operationally effective, and responsive to program objectives.


The role forms part of the SWLT's senior management structure and participates on Core Leadership Team meetings and strategic discussions as required, providing technical Leadership on industry, institutional strengthening and higher education engagement. The role works closely with the Principal, Stakeholders and Partnerships to ensure coordinated engagement, delivery, and alignment across institutional and industry-facing workstreams.


The position will be based in the DHERST office in Port Moresby and will require regular travel to provinces, partner institutions, industry sites, and other stakeholder engagement locations as required. The role will work also serves as a high-level strategic counterpart to DHERST Depurty Secretaries in advocating and advancing departmental engagement with business and industry to keep departmental learning focused on meeting employment demand.


Primary Responsibilities 


The primary responsibilities of the 
Team Leader - Industry and Institutions 
include:




Provide strategic leadership for Industry and Institutions workstreams under Outcomes 2, 3 and 4, ensuring alignment with SWLT objectives, implementation strategies and DHERST priorities.


Act as a senior engagement lead with DHERST, higher education institutions (HEIs), industry bodies, government agencies, development partners and implementing partners to strengthen partnerships, labour market engagement and institutional ownership.


Lead the planning, coordination and delivery of key workstreams, including grants management, HEI engagement, infrastructure support, leadership and management strengthening, and institutional capability development.


Ensure workplans, schedules, resources and delivery arrangements are realistic, coordinated and effectively implemented across multiple partners and delivery modalities.


Manage and supervise national and international staff, consultants and advisers, setting priorities, performance expectations and quality standards.


Oversee technical advisory inputs and ensure consistent, high-quality and accountable delivery of technical and operational activities.


Coordinate operational readiness, logistics and stakeholder engagement to support implementation across HEIs and partner organisations.


Monitor progress and performance, ensuring accurate reporting, evidence-based decision making and adaptive learning across Industry and Institutions activities.


Work closely with MERL personnel to capture outcomes, lessons learned and contributions to Outcomes 2, 3 and 4.


Manage delegated budgets, approve timesheets and invoices, monitor expenditure, provide forecasts and ensure financial compliance across grants and institutional investments.


Collaborate with Core Leadership Team members to support integrated planning, risk management, problem solving and program-wide decision making.


Ensure all activities incorporate gender equality, disability, social inclusion, locally led development, safeguarding, sustainability and other SWLT cross-cutting priorities.


Support the collection and use of disaggregated data and promote practical, ethical and inclusive systems, tools and reporting processes.


Contribute to continuous improvement, innovation and delivery of value in accordance with SWLT principles and organisational standards.


Comply with safeguarding, child protection and PSEAH requirements, report concerns promptly and uphold environmental sustainability commitments.




About you


You will have proven experience in the following areas:




Senior experience in institutional strengthening, higher education, or industry-linked skills development


Proven capability managing complex delivery programs across multiple institutions and partners


Experience leading and supervising multidisciplinary teams of national and international professionals


Strong understanding of government systems, stakeholder engagement, and politically informed programming


Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including strategic reporting and high-level stakeholder engagement


Strong operational and logistical management skills


Experience overseeing budgets, grants, and financial monitoring functions


Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team.


Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion.


Demonstrated commitment to inclusive, locally led, and adaptive development approaches.




To Apply


Please submit your application online at 
https://thepalladiumgroup.com/careers
, including your CV and detailed cover letter, outlining your suitability and experience in line with the requirements of the position.


Closing date: 
End of day Sunday 11
th
 October 2026. Candidates may be interviewed on a rolling basis.


Equity, Diversity & Inclusion -
 Palladium is committed to embedding equity, diversity, and inclusion into everything we do. We welcome applications from all sections of society and actively encourage diversity to drive innovation, creativity, success and good practice. We positively welcome and seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce; and that all job applicants and employees receive equal and fair treatment regardless of their background or personal characteristics. These include: (but are not limited to) socio-economic background, age, race, gender identity and expression, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, nationality, veteran, marital or Indigenous status.


Should you require any adjustments or accommodations to be made due to a disability or you are a neurodivergent individual or for any other circumstance, please email our team at 
[email protected]
 and we will be in touch to discuss.


Safeguarding -
 We define Safeguarding as “the preventative action taken by Palladium to protect our people, clients and the communities we work with from harm”. We are committed to ensuring that all children and adults who come into contact with Palladium are treated with respect and are free from abuse. All successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced selection process including safeguarding-focused interviews and a rigorous due diligence process.

In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.

Management of the diamond drill tooling, inventory and all related machinery and equipment.

28662.description:
Superintendent Financial Accounting


 


About Us


 
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.


The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual as 
Superintendent - Financial Accounting.


 


About the role


Reporting to the Finance Manager, the Superintendent Financial Accounting ensures the integrity and accuracy of financial reporting for the Porgera operation. The role leads the month-end close, manages audit deliverables, and supports fixed asset and treasury accounting. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring strong technical expertise, ownership of deliverables, and coaching of junior accountants.


In this role, you will:




Lead the month-end close and reporting process to ensure accuracy, completeness, and compliance with IFRS and corporate timelines.


Review and approve journals, reconciliations, and adjustments prepared by junior accountants.


Ensure balance sheet integrity through regular reconciliations, variance analysis, and timely resolution of unreconciled balances.


Coordinate the preparation of financial statements, reports, and supporting documentation for audits and management reviews.


Manage fixed assets and capital accounting, including capitalization, transfers, depreciation, and disposals.


Oversee cash flow accounting processes, intercompany reconciliations, and treasury transactions.


Coordinate bullion sales and revenue recognition.


Manage treasury and banking operations for all Porgera entities.


Provide support during internal and external audits, ensuring timely delivery of all audit requests.


Drive continuous improvement in accounting processes and ERP data integrity.


Coach and mentor junior team members to develop their technical and professional capabilities.




 


About You


You hold a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or Commerce and are CPA/CA certified (or equivalent). You have over 5 years of experience in financial accounting within mining or large-scale operations and a proven record of leading month-end processes and mentoring team members. You thrive in a fast-paced environment and demonstrate accountability, technical precision, and leadership by example.
 


Desirable:




Experience in a remote or FIFO mining environment.


Understanding of PNG tax and mining legislation.


Postgraduate qualifications in finance or business.




Preferred Systems Knowledge




SAP - FICO


Xeras


OneStream


Microsoft Excel


Oracle Account Reconciliation Cloud Service (ARCs)




Competencies and Skills




Financial Acumen: Strong understanding of financial accounting, treasury management and audit processes.


Business Partnering: Proven ability to build relationships with senior leaders and operational teams, drive financial accountability, and provide clear insights to help with decision-making.


Leadership and Team Development: The ability to lead a develop a high-performing team, providing mentorship and ensuring strong accountability.


Systems and Data Management: Proficiency in SAP FICO, Xeras, and OneStream, along with strong Excel skills for financial modeling and reporting process improvement.


Internal and External Audit: Proven experience managing the external audit for a large organization.




 


Mobilization Requirement 


In return, you will be joining a world-class mining operation with the opportunity to impact the development and upskilling of our predominantly local workforce, combined with a team keen to learn and absorb knowledge.  This offers a unique opportunity to further shape the department and improve NPL’s social performance and people knowledge. 


You will be joining an operation that values safety and lead a team towards best-in-class safety practices whilst contributing to the development of a highly capable national workforce, making a lasting impact on the industry.


This role is offered on a FIFO basis with a 21/14 roster and a highly competitive remuneration package.


 


Apply Now


If you’re ready to make your mark in a dynamic and supportive environment, submit your application today.


 


Closing Date: 10th October 2026






Apply

28517.description:
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE)


About the University


The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.


PNGUNRE operates across four locations:




Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to the University's core teaching, research and administrative functions.


Takubar Campus (Kokopo, East New Britain Province) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics.


Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training, applied learning and community development initiatives.


Momis Ocean and Climate Research Institute (MOCRI), Rabaul (East New Britain Province) – PNGUNRE's specialist hub for ocean and climate research, environmental monitoring, climate resilience, sustainable development, and national and international research collaboration.




The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, applied research, and strong partnerships with government, industry, communities and international institutions. Through its teaching, research and outreach activities, PNGUNRE develops graduates, knowledge and practical solutions that contribute to sustainable development in Papua New Guinea and the wider Pacific region.


About the Role


PNGUNRE invites applications from suitably qualified and experienced academics for appointment as 
Senior Lecturer – Ocean & Climate Research
 within the 
Momis Ocean and Climate Research Institute (MOCRI)
, based in Rabaul, East New Britain Province.


The position will provide senior academic and research expertise in ocean science, climate variability and change, marine environmental science, atmospheric processes, environmental monitoring, marine conservation, pollution, and climate and disaster risk.


The successful appointee will lead and contribute to research addressing the interaction between ocean, climate and marine systems and their implications for Papua New Guinea's natural resources, islands, coastal communities and sustainable development. The position will also contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, research supervision, scholarly publication and the development of collaborative research programs.


A key expectation of the role is to strengthen the University's research output and translate scientific findings into practical information that can support government, communities and other stakeholders in responding to ocean, climate and environmental challenges.


The position reports directly to the Dean – Momis Ocean and Climate Research Institute (MOCRI).


 


Key Responsibilities




Develop and lead research in ocean science, climate variability and change, marine environmental science and related areas.


Teach undergraduate and postgraduate courses in ocean, climate, atmospheric and environmental sciences.


Develop and review curricula, courses and teaching materials relevant to MOCRI's academic and research programs.


Supervise undergraduate, honours and postgraduate research projects and mentor junior academics and emerging researchers.


Lead and participate in multidisciplinary research projects addressing ocean-climate interactions, marine ecosystems, environmental change, pollution, conservation and climate and disaster risk.


Undertake field-based research and contribute to the collection, analysis and interpretation of ocean, climate and environmental data.


Publish research findings in reputable peer-reviewed and indexed journals and contribute other scholarly outputs relevant to Papua New Guinea and the Pacific.


Present research at national and international conferences, seminars and scientific forums.


Develop competitive research proposals and pursue external grants, consultancies and collaborative research opportunities.


Establish research partnerships with government agencies, communities, industry, NGOs, universities and national and international research institutions.


Work with relevant PNG government agencies and communities on ocean, climate and environmental research programs.


Provide scientific and technical advice to government and other stakeholders on ocean, climate, marine conservation, environmental risk and sustainable resource management.


Contribute research evidence and expertise to relevant policy discussions and submissions.


Participate in MOCRI and University academic governance, research planning, quality assurance and administrative activities.


Contribute to professional training, short courses, community outreach and other knowledge-transfer initiatives.




 


Qualifications, Experience, Skills & Experience


Applicants must demonstrate:




A PhD in Oceanography, Ocean Science, Climate Science, Marine Science, Atmospheric Science, Environmental Science, Earth Sciences, or a closely related discipline.


A minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional, academic or research experience in ocean, climate, marine or environmental sciences.


A demonstrated research record with five (5) or more publications in indexed peer-reviewed journals.


Demonstrated experience in tertiary or university-level teaching, curriculum development and student assessment.


Demonstrated capacity to supervise undergraduate and postgraduate research and mentor emerging researchers.


Strong research capability in one or more areas such as oceanography, ocean-climate interactions, climate variability, atmospheric science, marine environmental science, environmental monitoring, marine pollution or climate risk.


Experience in designing and undertaking field-based and applied scientific research.


Demonstrated ability to analyse and interpret scientific data and communicate research findings to academic and non-academic audiences.


Experience in developing research proposals and contributing to externally funded research, consultancy or multidisciplinary projects.


Strong academic writing, analytical, communication and project management skills.


Ability to translate research findings into practical information and technical advice for government, communities and other stakeholders.


Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and national and international research partners.


High standards of academic integrity, professional conduct and commitment to PNGUNRE's teaching, research and community engagement responsibilities.




 


Strategic Research Focus


PNGUNRE is particularly interested in candidates with demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following areas:




Oceanography and ocean science


Ocean-atmosphere interactions


Climate variability and climate change


Marine environmental science


Ocean and coastal monitoring


Sea-level change and coastal impacts


Marine ecosystems and conservation


Ocean and marine pollution


Climate modelling and environmental data analysis


Extreme weather and climate-related hazards


Climate and disaster risk management


Island and coastal resilience


Sustainable management of ocean and marine resources




 


Salary Range


Senior Lecturer 
Base Salary: PGK53,663.00 – PGK65,586.00 per annum
International Market Allowance: PGK52,062.00 – PGK63,354.00 per annum
(plus applicable allowances and benefits)


 


Why Join PNGUNRE?


This appointment offers an opportunity to take a leading role in developing ocean and climate research within the Momis Ocean and Climate Research Institute and to contribute to an area of considerable importance to Papua New Guinea and the wider Pacific.


Based in Rabaul, East New Britain Province, the position provides a unique setting for research into ocean, atmospheric, island and coastal systems. The successful candidate will have opportunities to establish multidisciplinary research programs, supervise postgraduate researchers, work with government and communities, and develop national and international research partnerships.


For an established ocean or climate researcher, the position provides an opportunity to help build PNGUNRE's research capability while generating knowledge that can contribute directly to climate resilience, environmental management and sustainable development in Papua New Guinea.


 


Living and Working in East New Britain


East New Britain offers a distinctive lifestyle alongside the professional opportunities available at PNGUNRE. The province is one of Papua New Guinea's established tourism destinations, known for its volcanic landscapes, tropical islands and coastlines, diving and snorkelling, rich cultural traditions, and significant World War II history. Rabaul and Kokopo provide access to places such as the Duke of York Islands, volcanic sites around Rabaul, historic war sites, beaches and marine environments.


For academics and researchers, East New Britain's natural environment also provides an exceptional setting for field-based teaching and research in agriculture, marine and coastal systems, climate, biodiversity, environmental management and sustainable development. Beyond work, staff can experience the province’s culture, islands, reefs, outdoor activities and community life.


 


Application Details


Interested applicants should submit:




A cover letter addressing suitability and relevant research expertise for the position


A detailed Curriculum Vitae, including a full list of research publications


Certified copies of academic and professional qualifications


Names and contact details of three (3) referees




Applications must be addressed to:


The Manager – Human Resources
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment
Vudal Campus, East New Britain Province
Email
: 
[email protected]


Closing Date: Friday, 09 October 2026


PNGUNRE is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from suitably qualified candidates. This position is open to both Papua New Guinean and international applicants.

The successful appointee will provide academic leadership in the development and delivery of undergraduate and postgraduate programs, lead applied and multidisciplinary research, supervise postgraduate students, mentor junior academics and contribute to building MOCRI's research profile.

A major focus of the position will be developing high-quality research programs that respond to the ocean, climate and marine environmental challenges facing Papua New Guinea and the Pacific.

Teach undergraduate and postgraduate courses and contribute to the development and review of programs in ocean, marine and environmental sciences.

Ten (10) or more years of relevant professional, academic and/or research experience, with substantial experience in ocean, marine, climate or environmental science.

Strong understanding of environmental and sustainable development policies, laws and institutional arrangements relevant to Papua New Guinea and the Pacific.

Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain partnerships with government, research institutions, development partners and other stakeholders.


Strong academic leadership, communication, mentoring and organisational skills.


Experience working in Papua New Guinea, the Pacific or other developing-country environments would be highly regarded.

28648.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


 


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


 


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


 










Your impact






As a Cost Controller, you'll track and manage costs across asset maintenance activities, helping maintain budget compliance, accurate cost allocation and clear financial reporting. You'll work with operational stakeholders to provide cost insights, strengthen budget ownership and identify opportunities to improve financial performance.










As part of our team, you will








Manage committed, incurred and forecast costs across assigned departments, including monitoring expenditure against budgets and completing detailed variance analysis.


Prepare monthly operating expenditure and capital expenditure accruals, cost allocations and financial reports, including cost reporting for operational stakeholders.


Maintain accurate cost records and reporting dashboards, including purchase orders, contractor claims, timesheets and vendor invoices.


Partner with superintendents, procurement, contractors and other stakeholders to resolve cost issues and strengthen understanding and ownership of budgets.


Identify opportunities to improve cost control processes and reporting efficiency while maintaining transparent records for audit and compliance requirements












Prerequisites for your success in this role








A Bachelor of Management, Bachelor of Accounting or related tertiary qualification; a Diploma in Accounting is also acceptable.


CPA or progressing towards CPA


Considerable experience in cost control, accounting, financial reporting or project controls.


Strong proficiency in SAP (S/4HANA), Power BI and Smartsheet reporting tools, with advanced Microsoft Excel skills.


Strong communication skills for working with suppliers, contractors and department managers, with the ability to work independently, meet deadlines and maintain accuracy under pressure.












Your work environment






This role is offered on a 28:14 Fly-in, Fly-out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, with ensuite, air-conditioned accommodation equipped with Wi-Fi, television and a mini fridge. A variety of nutritious meal options are available through on-site catering facilities, while recreational and social amenities provide opportunities to relax and connect with colleagues while on roster.


You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams supporting one of the world's largest gold mining operations, contributing to safe, reliable and sustainable performance in a technically complex and globally significant mining environment.


You'll be part of a team of six cost controllers supporting 15 departments, with responsibility for an assigned operational area and regular collaboration with superintendents on expenditure against budget and end-of-month reporting.










Why join Newmont






Lihir is one of the world's largest producing gold mines and one of Newmont's most significant operations.


Working at Lihir means joining a high-performing team committed to safety, operational excellence and delivering sustainable value for our people, communities and business. 


Eligible employees may benefit from:
•    Competitive salary and annual performance incentive opportunities.
•    Company-funded FIFO travel and modern camp accommodation.
•    Access to health, wellbeing and employee assistance programs.
•    Ongoing learning, technical development and leadership training opportunities.
•    Exposure to large-scale mining operations and industry-leading technologies.
•    Career opportunities across Newmont's Australian, Papua New Guinean and global operations.
•    Access to a diverse range of on-site recreational, dining and wellbeing facilities.
•    The opportunity to be part of a workplace where safety, inclusion and growth are at the centre of everything we do. 


Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 44873 before the advertised closing date: 8 October 2026.












At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​






Learn more about our purpose and values: 
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people: 
Life at Newmont
​






Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team: 
[email protected]
.

Project Engineer
Company: 
Reinhold Engineering and Group of Companies Limited
Location:

Reinhold Engineering and Group of Companies Limited is a nationally owned civil works and building construction company based in Port Moresby. As we continue to grow and strengthen our operations across Papua New Guinea, we are seeking a capable and experienced Administration Manager to lead and manage our administrative functions.


 


About the Role


The Project Engineer will oversee the day-to-day technical execution of construction or engineering projects. Be responsible for translating engineering designs into actionable site plans, managing resources, and ensuring all work complies with specifications, codes, and regulations. This role will be crucial in maintaining project momentum, solving on-site challenges, and fostering a collaborative environment among all project stakeholders.


 


Key Responsibilities




Manage and monitor overall project timelines, milestones, and critical paths to ensure on-schedule delivery.


Supervise and coordinate the activities of subcontractors and direct labour, ensuring work is performed according to contract documents and quality standards.


Conduct regular site inspections to verify compliance with engineering specifications, building codes, and safety regulations.


Attend and contribute to design coordination meetings, client reviews, and on-site progress meetings as required.


Communicate clearly and effectively with internal project teams, external subcontractors, suppliers, and client representatives.


Review and process technical submittals, shop drawings, and requests for information (RFIs).


Implement and enforce strict site safety protocols and quality control procedures.


Provide hands-on technical guidance and problem-solving support to resolve construction and engineering issues.


Maintain accurate and comprehensive project documentation, including daily reports, progress photos, and as-built drawings.




 


Qualifications and Experience




Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering


Preferablya registered member of Institute of Engineers PNG Inc. (IEPNG)


Minimum of 5 years progressive experience in the civil engineering and construction industry


Minimum of 5 years experience as a Project Engineer


Ability to lead, coordinate and motivate a multi-disciplined workforce


Strong knowledge of PNG Codes (Building Act, MRA Act)


Strong written and verbal communication skills


Must have a Class 3 Driver’s License




 


 
Key Competencies




Exceptional leadership and team management abilities, with a focus on mentoring and developing talent.


Superior communication, negotiation, and client relationship management skills.


Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a keen attention to detail.


In-depth knowledge of construction methods, materials, and legal regulations.


Ability to read and interpret complex engineering drawings, blueprints, and specifications.


Proficiency in standard office software suites and industry-specific applications.


Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to address site challenges proactively.




 


 


What We Offer




Competitive remuneration package


Opportunity to contribute to a growing nationally owned company


Professional and respectful working environment


Opportunity to play a key role in strengthening organizational systems

28449.description:
Own network architecture, security and NOC performance
Hands-on Cisco/Fortinet expertise essential
Lead and mentor a 24/7 network operations team
About the Company
 This bank delivers secure and innovative digital banking solutions across Papua New Guinea, supporting individuals and businesses through modern, always-on digital channels including mobile, internet, USSD and agency banking.
 
About the Role
 Reporting to the Head of IT, the Senior Manager, Network Infrastructure owns the availability, performance and security of the network underpinning the bank's LAN, WAN and digital banking channels — mobile app, internet banking, USSD, agency banking, card/ATM/POS switching and API/Open Banking integrations. This is a genuinely senior, hands-on role: you'll lead the Network Operations Centre (NOC), take real ownership of the network domain, and be accountable for resilient, secure infrastructure in a 24/7/365 banking environment.
 
Key Responsibilities
 
 
Own network architecture and ensure 24/7/365 availability across all digital banking channels
 
Lead the NOC, driving proactive monitoring and rapid incident resolution
 
Develop and enforce network security controls aligned with Central Bank guidelines, PCI-DSS and ISO 27001
 
Manage capacity planning to maintain resilience during peak transaction periods
 
Lead network-related projects supporting new digital products and channel expansion
 
Manage vendor, telco and payment ecosystem relationships and SLAs
 
Own the network operations budget and reporting
 
Lead, mentor and develop the network operations and NOC team, including 24/7 shift coverage
 
Maintain network documentation, DR/BCP plans and drive regular DR/failover testing
 
Stay current with emerging network, security and fintech infrastructure trends
 
 
Key Requirements & Qualifications
 
 
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, IT, Telecommunications or related field; Master's an advantage
 
Hands-on experience with Cisco and Fortinet platforms is essential
 
Professional certifications such as CCNP/CCIE, JNCIP, ITIL, CISSP/CISM strongly preferred
 
8–10+ years in network engineering/operations, including 3–5 years in a genuine senior management role with domain ownership — not purely technical delivery
 
Proven experience managing network infrastructure supporting core banking, digital/mobile channels and payment switching (ATM/POS/card networks)
 
Strong, current knowledge of network security, firewalls, routing/switching, DDoS mitigation and SIEM tooling, plus awareness of emerging network technologies
 
Proven track record leading and developing teams, ideally in a 24/7 NOC or operations environment
 
Working knowledge of banking/payment regulatory frameworks (Central Bank guidelines, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001)
 
 
This is a senior, high-impact role for a network leader ready to take true ownership of a bank's digital infrastructure
 — shaping strategy, leading a 24/7 team, and directly protecting the customer experience across every digital channel.

You will lead a corporate and client service operations business unit — overseeing AGM coordination, board and statutory reporting, and governance frameworks — while also driving service delivery, financial performance, and revenue growth.
 
 As the senior relationship and governance lead, you will manage interactions with corporate clients, government agencies, and regulatory bodies, ensuring board and statutory reporting obligations are met, while identifying market opportunities to enhance service offerings and maximize commercial performance.

Provide company secretarial and corporate governance leadership, including AGM coordination, board and statutory reporting, and governance framework oversight.

28079.description:
PNG Air, renowned for its extensive network covering over 26 destinations throughout Papua New Guinea, operates the largest fleet of ATR 72-600 & ATR 42-600 series aircraft in the region. As the Airline of Choice, we're committed to delivering a world-class experience with competitive fares, unparalleled cargo rates, and a focus on safety and on-time performance for our valued customers and stakeholders.


 


CREDIT CONTROLLER


 


PNG Air is seeking a suitably qualified and experienced 
Credit Controller
 to join its Finance Department based in Port Moresby.


 


Reporting to the 
Financial Controller
, with oversight from the 
Chief Financial Officer
, the Credit Controller is responsible for managing the Company's accounts receivable portfolio, minimizing credit risk, improving cash collections and ensuring customers comply with agreed trading terms. The role is critical in maintaining healthy cashflow through proactive debtor management, timely collection of outstanding accounts and effective stakeholder engagement with both internal and external customers.


 


The incumbent will work closely with Commercial, Charter, Freight, Customer Service and Finance teams to ensure accurate billing, prompt resolution of customer disputes and effective credit management across PNG Air and its subsidiaries. The role also supports continuous improvement of credit policies, reporting and internal controls to safeguard company assets and reduce bad debt exposure.


 


 


 
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 


Accounts Receivable & Collections




Ensure customer invoices are issued accurately and on time.


Proactively manage the collection of outstanding accounts through telephone, email, written correspondence and customer visits where required.


Ensure debts are collected within agreed payment terms and actively reduce overdue receivables.


Monitor daily receipts and ensure customer payments are allocated accurately.


Follow up disputed invoices promptly and work with internal stakeholders to achieve timely resolution.


Recommend legal recovery actions where collection efforts have been exhausted.


Prepare recommendations for bad debt provisions and write-offs for management approval.




Cashflow Management




Support the Company's cashflow objectives by improving debtor collections and reducing Days Sales Outstanding (DSO).


Monitor debtor ageing trends and identify emerging collection risks.


Assist Management in achieving monthly cash collection and debtor reduction targets.


Identify deteriorating payment patterns and recommend corrective action.




Reporting & Analysis




Prepare weekly debtor reports for the Chief Financial Officer and Financial Controller.


Prepare monthly Accounts Receivable and Aged Debtors reports for PNG Air and its subsidiaries.


Report significant overdue accounts, disputed balances and collection risks.


Provide management with accurate debtor forecasts and collection updates.


Produce ad hoc financial reports and analysis as requested.




Customer Relationship Management




Maintain professional relationships with customers while ensuring Company credit policies are enforced.


Respond promptly to customer enquiries relating to invoices, statements and account balances.


Work collaboratively with Commercial, Sales, Charter and Freight departments to resolve billing issues.


Ensure customer statements are distributed monthly and account queries are resolved efficiently.




Financial Controls & Compliance




Ensure all credit management activities comply with PNG Air policies, financial delegations and internal controls.


Maintain complete audit trails supporting receivable balances and collection activities.


Assist during internal and external audits by providing supporting documentation and explanations.


Ensure all customer accounts are reconciled regularly and reconciling items investigated promptly.


Support continuous improvement of credit control procedures and systems.




 


QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCES


 




Bachelor's Degree or quivalent in Accounting, Finance, Business, Commerce or a related discipline.


Minimum three (3) years' experience in Credit Control, Accounts Receivable or Finance.


Previous experience within the aviation industry or a large commercial organisation will be highly regarded.


Strong understanding of credit management principles, debtor collections and cashflow management.


Experience in customer account reconciliations and dispute resolution.


Working knowledge of accounting systems such as Sage 300 or equivalent ERP systems.


Advanced Microsoft Excel skills with strong analytical capability.


Demonstrated ability to prepare accurate financial reports and debtor analysis.




 


If you feel you meet our requirements and are interested, we would like to hear from you. Send your application in only one PDF file to:


 


[email protected]


 


Applications close: 
Friday 09th October 2026


Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.


 


We are an equal opportunity employer.

27921.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


This position is responsible for the service and maintenance of heavy surface equipment in a safe and appropriate manner. This includes Trucks, Drills, Front-end loaders, Dozers, Mobile cranes (45T & 100T), and other pieces of equipment.


Key Accountabilities




Undertaking scheduled servicing and preventative maintenance of the company's heavy vehicle fleet, including Sandvik, CAT and Normet vehicles and equipment.


Respond to machinery breakdowns promptly and undertake quality repairs in a timely manner.


Servicing and preventative maintenance on Jumbos, Loaders and Trucks.


Diagnosis and troubleshooting of faults, and recommending servicing interventions that improve the operational efficiency of the company's heavy vehicle fleet


Rectifying machinery breakdowns in an underground environment promptly and undertake quality repairs in a timely manner.


Ensuring completion of all shift paperwork including service sheets, work orders and daily shift reports.


Completing all JSA's, risk assessments and documentation to ensure all work is completed safely and as per schedule. 


Give direction, coaching and technical assistance to Trade Assistant’s and apprentice.




About You 


Qualifications & Experience


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a NATTB certified Trade Certificate in Heavy Equipment Fitting with 3+ years’ experience in mining environment or heavy construction industry. In addition to this, you will have




Experience with Mining Equipment like Drills, LHD Loaders, Caterpillar Equipment, Sandvik Equipment etc.


Experience fitter with hydraulics training background.


Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.


Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.


Excellent trouble shooting skills.


Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.


Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.


Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

28610.description:
About Lihir


Lihir is one of the world's largest gold mining operations, located on Niolam Island in Papua New Guinea's New Ireland Province. The operation is renowned for its unique volcanic landscape and combines world-class mining and processing with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability,  innovation and technical excellence.


The operation combines open-pit mining and gold processing in a remote island setting, supported by modern facilities and a culture focused on improving daily.


At Lihir, you'll be part of a team that is deeply connected to the island and the communities that call it home. We are committed to creating lasting benefits through local employment, training, scholarships and apprenticeship programs, while fostering a workplace where people look out for one another and succeed together.


With a culture grounded in safety, respect and delivering responsibly, Lihir offers the opportunity to develop your career while contributing to an operation that plays an important role in Papua New Guinea's economic and social development.










Your Impact






As a Metallurgist, you'll provide technical support and metallurgical expertise to help achieve optimum and cost-effective plant performance within Processing while maximising gold recovery. You'll work closely with operational and maintenance teams to analyse performance, support plant stability, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.










As part of our team, you will








Provide technical support to Processing Operations through metallurgical analysis, reporting and performance evaluation of plant circuits, equipment and systems.


Collaborate with maintenance teams to improve process plant equipment and instrument performance and availability.


Support plant stability by working closely with operational personnel and key stakeholders across the business.


Design, manage and execute plant trials, surveys and metallurgical test work to support operational performance and improvement initiatives.


Identify process improvement and cost reduction opportunities while supporting safe and effective metallurgical performance outcomes.












Prerequisites for your success in this role








Bachelor's degree in Mineral Processing, Metallurgy or a related discipline.


Experience as a site-based metallurgist in a mining or mineral processing environment.


Demonstrated knowledge of metallurgical processes, laboratory operations and metallurgical accounting within a large-scale mining environment.


Strong analytical, problem-solving and planning skills, with the ability to work autonomously and manage competing priorities.


Effective communication, interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills, with proficiency in Microsoft Office and process monitoring systems.












Your work environment






This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly-in, Fly-out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.


Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp environment, with ensuite, air-conditioned accommodation equipped with a mini fridge, television and Wi-Fi. A variety of nutritious meal options are available through the on-site catering facilities, while recreational and social amenities provide opportunities to relax and connect with colleagues while on roster.


Based at Lihir within the Process Plant Metallurgy team, this role reports to the Supervisor Metallurgy and has no direct reports. The role works closely with Processing, Maintenance and other technical stakeholders to support metallurgical performance and operational outcomes.










Why join Newmont






Lihir is one of the world's largest producing gold mines and one of Newmont's most significant operations.


Working at Lihir means joining a high-performing team committed to safety, operational excellence and delivering sustainable value for our people, communities and business. 


Eligible employees may benefit from:
•    Competitive salary and annual performance incentive opportunities.
•    Company-funded FIFO travel and modern camp accommodation.
•    Access to health, wellbeing and employee assistance programs.
•    Ongoing learning, technical development and leadership training opportunities.
•    Exposure to large-scale mining operations and industry-leading technologies.
•    Career opportunities across Newmont's Australian, Papua New Guinean and global operations.
•    Access to a diverse range of on-site recreational, dining and wellbeing facilities.
•    The opportunity to be part of a workplace where safety, inclusion and growth are at the centre of everything we do. 


Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 43425 before the advertised closing date: 8 October 2026.














We are seeking a motivated Metallurgist to join our Processing team at Lihir Gold Mine, one of the world's largest gold mining operations. 






As a Metallurgist, you will play a critical role in optimizing plant performance and maximizing gold recovery. Working closely with Processing Operations, Maintenance, and Mining teams, you will provide technical support, troubleshoot metallurgical issues, and drive continuous improvement initiatives to achieve production and budget targets. 






This is an exciting opportunity for an early to mid-career metallurgist looking to develop their technical expertise within a large-scale, complex gold processing operation. 






Key Responsibilities 










Monitor and optimize plant performance to maximize gold production and recovery. 














Ensure operating parameters and metallurgical targets are achieved. 














Provide technical guidance and support to Operations teams. 














Investigate and resolve metallurgical and process-related issues. 














Collaborate with Mining teams to support ore planning and ore delivery. 














Analyze plant performance data and identify improvement opportunities. 














Develop and recommend process optimization initiatives. 














Support metallurgical accounting, reporting, and reconciliation activities. 














Contribute to achieving production, recovery, safety, and cost objectives. 










About You 










You are a collaborative and analytical professional with a passion for continuous improvement and operational excellence. 






Required Qualifications & Experience 










Bachelor's degree in metallurgical engineering, Mineral Processing, Chemical Engineering, or related discipline. 














3–10 years' experience in a metallurgical or mineral processing environment, preferably within gold processing. 














Strong understanding of metallurgical processes and plant operations. 














Experience analyzing process data and implementing performance improvements. 














Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills. 














Ability to build strong working relationships across Operations, Maintenance, and Mining teams. 














Strong communication and technical reporting skills. 










If you feel that you could make a meaningful contribution in this role, we encourage you to discuss this opportunity with your current people leader and how it aligns with your longer term career goals.

If you have issues applying through Discovery or would like to learn more about the role before applying, please contact the relevant member of our Talent Acquisition Team.
