The incumbent manages the day-to-day operation of travel services and camp facilities, including accommodation, laundry and kitchen services. This responsibility includes maintaining high standards of hygiene, health and safety for all workers.


The role also manages travel and hotel accommodation bookings, enforces the travel policy, and ensures that domestic and international travel and company charter bookings are completed accurately and on time in accordance with company rosters.

Safety

Essential

Experience working on FIFO roles


Previous relevant work experience in mining or heavy industry, on site.


Excellent computer, communication and writing skills.


Computer literacy with Microsoft Products particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint


Open, honest and a Team Player




Desirable




Working with people of diverse backgrounds


Open to people and willing to help outside of usual responsibilities

This is a FIFO position, the roster will be 28 days on, and 14 days off with weekend work.


Betel nut and alcohol is not tolerated, as per company Policy.


All PPE given out remains the property of WML and must be worn whilst at work. Loss, theft or undue damage to issued PPE will remain the responsibility of the employee.

Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.


Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.


About the role


 


Gold room Operators are skilled technicians responsible for the day-to-day operation of the gold room and gravity recovery circuits including the;
• Gravity recovery processes including Falcon Concentrator and shaking tables
• Calcining and smelting of concentrate to dore
• Maintaining the highest levels of product security and accurate record keeping.
• Operational management of the tails storage facility and return water.


Key / Major Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.


• Perform the day-to-day operation of the gold room and TSF including;
o Gravity recovery circuit comprising scalping screen, Falcon concentrator, shaking tables
o Calcining and smelting of concentrate to dore
o Preparation of required reagents
o Management of tailings deposition and plant return water systems
o Management of off-site water discharges from the TSF
o Dore shipment


 


About You 


To be considered for this role, you must have a minimum of Grade 10 school Certificate with good personal attributes, and 3 years’ experience in gold room operation. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.


• Valid PNG Class 3 license (essential)
• Machinery license's including loader, skid steer, telehandler (desirable)
• Previous experience in a process plant (desirable).
• An appropriate trades trade certificate (desirable)
• You must be physically fit
• to enjoy practical and manual activities
• to be able to read and follow written instructions in English.
• the ability to work as part of a team.
• good hand-eye co-ordination


 


Life at K92  


Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Joining our APD team, you will work coordinate a team of APD officers to ensure the safety of our growing gold site in the Eastern Highlands. In this role you will assist with the development of operational security systems, develop standard operating procedures, and provide training in security emergency related preparedness


Key Accountabilities




Proactively engage with the APD Supervisors to provide security advice and support to the APD Teams to ensure APD fleet availability and security targets are achieved and optimised against budget.


Respond to routine and emergency calls for security /or support within the mine site area, underground or in the field as required to ensure security on equipment and people`s life is minimised.


Perform troubleshooting to identify and remedy issues that may arise.


Support and assist the APD team to ensure the rectification of identified defect equipment to improve and optimise availability and reliability targets.


Work closely with the Superintendent APD to assess performance and identify improvement projects to maximise results, reduce risk and implement cost management initiatives.


Maintain the Gold Room security system and ensure that the contract between the owners and contractors relating to the movement of gold, is carried out in accordance with K92 Mining Limited`s procedures.


Establish a high-performance culture by motivating team members to achieve a high level of performance and by rewarding and recognising high performance.

Ensure effective processes for communicating relevant information, including company, site, department, and team performance, to all team members are in place.


Direct and train employees on the APD process, procedure, and Equipment.


Continuously mentor and coach technicians on effective repair techniques.


Identify skills gaps and training requirements and assist in developing training packages as required to close the skills gap.


Actively review the work performance of APD Supervisors and provide feedback to the APD Superintendent including the talent and succession planning for designated key roles.


Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.


Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.

 Successful completion of accredited safety, fire, and emergency response training.


Competent in breathing apparatus, rescue from height, confined space rescue and fire response.


Experience in fire suppression equipment maintenance.


Current Occupational First Aid Certificate.


Good written and oral communication skills in English and Pidgin.


Ability to write reports and have good computer skills in Word & Excel.


Proven man management and supervisory skills.


Good, demonstrated skills in Radio / telephone procedures.


Sound incident investigation skills.


Truck driving license.


Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.


Excellent trouble shooting skills.


Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.


Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.

Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.

Porgera | Officer – Asset Protection (242204)






Porgera, Enga, Papua New Guinea
























 


























Job Description




About Us


New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.


 


The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual as 
Asset Protection Officer – APD (NS_242204)


 
About the role


Reporting to the 
Chief Duty Officer (CDO)
, the Asset Protection officer will be supervising local security employees in their day-to-day function as well as providing security to the New Porgera mine site and its associated installations. The role is to maintain Security across the Mining Operations by monitoring and reporting of civil disturbances and breaches of safety and other company policies. A high level of competency is required. This role is an operational field role requiring team work.


In this role, you will:


•    Maintain Security across the Mining Operations 
•    Carry out tasks as directed by the Chief Duty Officer or Superintendent
•    Must be able to communicate effectively with Security Control during shifts
•    Maintain production by responding to security threats and incidents
•    Maintain security and safety for all personnel and company property 
•    Management and support on methods to minimize security risk from internal and external theft of company assets and provide comprehensive report and recommendation to management and or Police.
•    Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.


 


About You


To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
•    Have a minimum of Grade 10 Certificate or higher
•    Have a minimum of 6 years Police/Military experience 
•    Be Physically fit and able to walk on your feet for extended periods

28148.description:
Summary






The selected candidate will oversee all accounting operations, including accounts payable, receivable, and financial reporting. This role involves managing a team of accountants to ensure accurate recording of financial transactions, compliance with tax regulations, and preparation of audit materials. S/he will specifically focus on accounting functions and collaborate with the Finance Department on related financial planning and analysis activities.


Duties and Responsibilities






1) Accounting Operations (AP, AR, GL)




Oversee accounts payable and receivable processes to ensure timely and accurate processing of payments, receipts, and allocations.


Ensure customer and vendor reconciliations are performed and reviewed, including monitoring of aging reports and follow-up actions.


Maintain accurate general ledger postings and ensure proper supporting documentation for all transactions.


Manage month-end close activities, including review of journals, accruals, prepayments, and account reconciliations.




2) Retail Accounting and POS Control




Ensure monthly billing and retail sales reporting is complete and accurate.


Reconcile point-of-sale (POS) data to accounting records and investigate variances with Retail Operations.


Monitor inventory accounting movements and support inventory turnover reporting and reconciliation.




3) Financial Reporting (Preparation and Accuracy)




Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in line with IFRS/GAAP and company policies.


Prepare monthly management reports, including P&L statements and key supporting schedules for review by the CFO/Financial Controller.


Ensure financial reports are complete, accurate, and supported by reconciliation schedules before submission for internal review.




4) Operational Financial Controls (Monitor and Escalate)




Implement and enforce accounting policies and procedures to safeguard assets and maintain financial integrity.


Ensure segregation of duties is applied within AP, AR, cash handling, POS processes, and journal approvals.


Review high-risk areas and exception items, including manual journal entries, credit notes, write-offs, adjustments, refunds, and unusual vendor/customer activity.


Perform variance and exception reviews (e.g., unusual movements, out-of-pattern transactions, repeated overrides) and document findings.


Escalate suspicious transactions, control breaches, or significant variances to the CFO/Financial Controller and support follow-up actions.


Support Internal Audit by providing documents, explanations, and evidence of control performance (without compromising audit independence).




5) Tax and Statutory Compliance




Ensure compliance with tax regulations, including preparation and filing of corporate tax returns, VAT/GST, and payroll-related taxes where applicable.


Maintain accurate tax working papers and coordinate with tax consultants and authorities as required.


Ensure adherence to applicable IAS and local regulatory requirements.




6) Audit Coordination and Close-Out




Serve as the main contact for external auditors for accounting matters.


Prepare audit schedules and provide supporting documents and explanations in a timely manner.


Track audit findings and implement agreed corrective actions within Finance to strengthen controls and improve compliance.




7) Systems, Process Improvement, and Data Integrity




Ensure accounting systems and processes are optimised for accuracy, efficiency, and proper access control.


Work with IT and relevant departments to improve integration between ERP/accounting systems and other platforms (including POS).


Maintain proper master data controls (customers, vendors, chart of accounts) and data integrity within systems.




8) Team Leadership and Capability Building




Lead and develop the accounting team to ensure effective delivery of daily operations and month-end close.


Assign responsibilities, monitor performance, and ensure staff follow SOPs and control procedures.


Conduct performance reviews and provide coaching and training to improve skills and compliance.


Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, and professionalism within the department.




Job Requirements








CPA or ACCA or equivalent professional accounting certification (required).


Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field (required).


Minimum 10 years of accounting experience, with at least 2 years in a supervisory or management role.


Proven experience managing AP, AR, general ledger, and month-end close.


Experience supporting retail accounting operations, including POS reconciliations and P&L reporting.


Experience supporting audits and implementing corrective actions from findings.


Strong knowledge of IFRS/GAAP, tax regulations, and audit requirements.


Proficiency with accounting software and ERP systems; familiarity with retail POS systems.


Strong skills in reconciliations, reporting, and operational control monitoring.


High attention to detail and strong quality control habits.


Strong leadership and team management capability.


Strong analytical skills with ability to identify exceptions and control issues.


Clear communication skills and ability to escalate issues with evidence and recommendations.


Strong organisation and ability to manage deadlines and multiple priorities.

28599.description:
VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT 


 


Position: Monitoring, Evaluation, Reflection and Learning (MERL) Coordinator for the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea 


Reporting to: 
Church Partnership Program Coordinator


The Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea (ACPNG), part of the worldwide Anglican Communion, continues to contribute significantly to the development of Papua New Guinea.


Through its Church Partnership Program (CPP), funded by the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs & Trade (DFAT) in collaboration with Anglican Board of Mission (ABM) and Anglicans in Development (AID), ACPNG values equality and inclusiveness, and encourages qualified individuals to apply.


Position Summary


The MERL Coordinator will oversee the monitoring, evaluation, reflection and learning functions of ACPNG’s Church Partnership Program, assessing impact and supporting program improvement. This includes design & implementation of MERL systems, data analysis, quality evidence-based reporting and communications. This role also includes responsibility for coordination of organisational capacity development activities, in collaboration with ACPNG’s National Office and CPP Coordinator.


Key Responsibilities and Skills




Develop and implement a comprehensive MERL system that captures key performance indicators and outcomes of ACPNG’s Church Partnership Program. In addition, support ACPNG to develop a broader MERL system for ministry arms’ development programs.


Collect and analyse data from various sources, including surveys, interviews, focus groups, and performance reports, to assess the impact and effectiveness of ACPNG’s Church Partnership Program.


Support the CPP Coordinator in program design processes including drafting proposals and annual plans


Prepare regular progress reports, present findings, and share lessons learned with stakeholders, including the national church, partner churches, and development organizations.


Facilitate regular reflection and learning sessions to identify best practices, challenges, and opportunities for improvement within ACPNG’s Church Partnership Program.


Design and deliver training programs for CPP staff and volunteers to build their skills and knowledge in monitoring, evaluation, reflection, and learning.


Research and advocacy: Stay informed about emerging trends and best practices in community development, and advocate for the integration of these practices within the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea.


Coordinate the implementation of ACPNG’s organisational capacity development plans, in collaboration with the CPP Coordinator and ACPNG’s National Office and in line with the CPP Capacity Action Plan and ACPNG Strategic Plan  


Conduct MERL visits to ACPNG’s Church Partnership Program activities (domestically) for up to 4 weeks per year.


Provide MERL support for ACPNG humanitarian responses




 


Qualifications and Experience 




A relevant degree in MERL or a related field


Minimum of 5 years’ experience in MERL within the non-profit sector, including collecting data and writing reports, preferably related to community development, humanitarian response or social services.


Familiarity with the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea and its programs and initiatives, or a willingness to learn and adapt quickly.


Previous experience with Kobo Toolbox, Folktale or other data tracking software


Excellent communication (verbal and written), interpersonal, and teamwork skills, with the ability to build and maintain relationships with various stakeholders.


Knowledge of disability inclusion, gender equity, adult literacy, finance and/or community-based organisations would be looked upon favourably


Experience in photography and/or videography for communications, advocacy, or development programs would be an advantage.


Willingness to travel domestically for up to 4 weeks per year




Contract Duration




Up to December 2027, renewable based on performance and funding.


Other conditions: As per ACPNG HR policies.


Remuneration Package will be discussed during interview




Other Requirements 




Police Clearance Certificate (issued within the last 6 months) required

28748.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


In this role you will process and monitor payment expenditures so that vendors and Service Providers are paid within the established credit term limits. Moreover, this role involves performing high standards of accountability and transparency in all business dealings with the various vendors.


Key / Major Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.


 •             Receive all creditors’ invoices and statements as they come in.


•              Collate invoices with the relevant Purchase orders and Purchase Requisitions.


•              Providing accounts, administrative and clerical services.


•              Reconcile creditor’s statements as they are received with the relevant invoices and payment details.


•              Voucher match (VM) invoices with Purchase Orders for each supplier in the computer system using Pronto Accounting Software.


•              Ensure correct authorization of invoices and related documents before processing and payment onto Pronto.


•              Process all creditors payments (both local and overseas) and general ledger entries as required.


•              Address all creditors enquiries regarding their account and have all matters resolved in a timely manner to maintain good business standing.


•              Distribute remittance advices to Suppliers and Service Providers on a timely basis.


•              Refer immediately to the Senior Accountant any matters that is deemed beyond the scope of responsibility of the position so that these matters may be dealt with appropriately.


•              Ensure all accounts paid files are properly filed, tagged and stored where they can easily be retrieved and researched in future.


•              Maintain a good record of filing and labelling system for all unprocessed invoices and statements where they can be easily retrieved for further action where required.


•              Assist subordinates as and when required.


•              Brief Senior Accountant on a regular basis on accounts matters and work plan for a scheduled period e.g., weekly, fortnightly etc. and any matters that may need special attention to.


•              Maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with government and company policy.


•              Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.


•              Disburses petty cash by recording entry and verifying documentation.


•              Protects organization's value by keeping information confidential.


•              Able to provide Aged Trail Balance at any point in time and at month end.


About You 


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a


•              A Degree or Diploma in accounting or related field.


•              At least 5 years’ experience in a mining environment.


•              Experience in Pronto Accounting system is preferred.


•              Be a self-starter, very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems


•              Flexible and adaptable and be a team player.


•              Well versed in general accounting and banking procedures/systems or functions.


•              Ability to meet communicated schedules and deadlines.


•              Strong planning and organizational skills.


•              Proficient in computer and e-mail correspondences and courteous.


•              Ability to maintain good working relationships with vendors and other stakeholders.


Life at K92  


Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 






Apply

Communications Coordinator
 to be based in 
Mt.Hagen, Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea.


 


PURPOSE OF THE POSITION


The Communications Coordinator leads strategic communications and public engagement for the Sustainable Highlands Region Core Road Network Project. Based in Western Highlands, the role documents and promotes the project’s progress and impact through compelling stories, photographs, videos, case studies, and other communication products while ensuring compliance with donor branding requirements. It also strengthens stakeholder awareness and trust by supporting media engagement, public events, community campaigns, staff capacity-building, and emergency communications.


MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Regular field visits to target communities to capture progress and impact stories

Support and advise Project team in participation of relevant public events in Highland Region


Work with Project team to develop Comms & Public Engagement plan for the Project


Ensure coordination with Communications team in National Office to maximize support and guidance for compelling content being delivered by efficient workflows, assuring wise stewardship


Lead and advise if any ceremony, launch, opening or closing events linked to Project.


Provide content to NO Comms team for posting in newspaper, WVPNG social media accounts


Support IEC material and resource development linked to project campaign and/or community awareness raising


Support preparation of presentation materials during reflection and M&E events.


Support emergency communication and content generation in case of natural disasters and conflicts in project sites


Support story and photo collection in case of emergency response.




EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE

Minimum 3 years of relevant experience


Advanced communications technical skills such as photo and video production, editorial, graphic design, and media relations.

Advanced level of computer proficiency, Mac and PC, including editing skills across Adobe and Apple software for video, photo, media, design.

Build capability. Develop people. Strengthen performance.


 


Islands Petroleum is seeking a motivated and highly organised 
Learning & Development Coordinator
 to help build the capability of our people across the business.


Reporting to the 
HR & Talent Development Manager
, this role will coordinate and support the delivery of leadership and professional development programs across our operations. You will work closely with managers, depot teams, employees and external training providers to ensure our people have the skills, knowledge and competencies required to perform effectively, safely and in line with business requirements.


 


What you'll be responsible for


In this role, you will:




Coordinate and administer soft-skills training programs and support operational teams to deliver technical, safety, compliance training.

At least 5 years' relevant experience, ideally within the petroleum industry or a similar operational environment.


Strong organisational, planning and coordination skills.


Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.


The ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.


Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint.


Experience working with LMS or HRIS systems.


A sound understanding of adult learning principles and training methodologies.


A positive attitude, professional behaviour and a strong commitment to working safely.

Higher training completion rates


Stronger competency compliance


Increased employee participation


Timely delivery of training programs


Improved workforce capability and performance
.

28576.description:
HR Business Partner – Momase




 


Partner with the business. Strengthen leaders. Build workforce capability.


 


Islands Petroleum is seeking an experienced and commercially minded 
HR Business Partner - Momase 
to join our Human Resources team in Lae.


This is an opportunity for an HR professional who wants to work close to the business-partnering directly with operational leaders, understanding workforce challenges and translating business priorities into practical people solutions.


Reporting to the 
HR & Talent Development Manager,
 you will support leaders across the Momase region to strengthen leadership effectiveness, build workforce capability, improve employee performance and engagement, and proactively manage people-related risks.


 


The opportunity:


This is not simply an HR administration role.


As an HR Business Partner, you will be expected to understand the operational environment, build trusted relationships with leaders and use your HR expertise, judgement and workforce insights to influence better people and business outcomes.


You will play an important role across the entire employee lifecycle-from workforce planning and recruitment through to performance, talent development, employee relations, organisational change and succession.


 


Key Responsibilities: 






Translate business priorities and workforce challenges into practical people plans and HR solutions.


Provide trusted, evidence-based advice to leaders on workforce, organisational and employee matters.


Coach and challenge leaders to strengthen leadership practices, accountability and people management.


Support talent reviews, succession planning, critical-role pipelines and workforce capability development.


Partner with Learning & Development on development plans, leadership programs and targeted capability initiatives.


Strengthen performance management, objective setting, accountability and continuous feedback.


Provide advice and support on employee relations, grievances, disciplinary matters, investigations and workplace conflict.


Partner with Talent Acquisition and hiring managers on workforce requirements, recruitment priorities and quality of hire.


Support effective onboarding, internal mobility and retention of critical talent.


Ensure HR practices remain aligned with company policy and applicable PNG employment legislation.


Use HR data and workforce analytics to identify trends, risks and opportunities and support evidence-based decision making.


Support organisational change, restructuring, growth initiatives and change communication.


Reinforce Islands Petroleum's commitment to safety, employee wellbeing and sustainable workforce practices.




 


What we're looking for


We are looking for an HR professional who can operate confidently with managers and employees while maintaining sound judgement, credibility and professionalism.


 


You will ideally bring:




A Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organisational Psychology or a related discipline.


A relevant HR professional qualification or certification would be advantageous.


5-7 years of progressive HR experience, including HR Business Partnering or HR Advisory experience.


Experience supporting an operational, industrial, logistics, retail, fuel distribution, petroleum, mining or similarly complex environment.


Demonstrated experience partnering with operational managers and business leaders.


Strong practical experience across employee relations, performance management, workforce planning and organisational development.


Experience using HR information systems, workforce data and people analytics to support decision making.




 


You'll be well suited to this role if you can…




Think commercially
 - understand what the business is trying to achieve and translate that into practical workforce solutions.


Build credibility with leaders
 - become a trusted adviser who can coach, influence and appropriately challenge.


Navigate complex people matters
 - provide balanced, consistent and practical advice while managing organisational and employee risk.


Use data to tell the workforce story
 - move beyond transactional reporting and use people insights to support better decisions.


Develop capability for the future
 - help strengthen leadership pipelines, succession coverage, internal mobility and employee development.


Lead through change
 - support managers and employees through organisational growth, restructuring and operational change.




 


If you are an experienced HR professional who enjoys being close to operations, working with leaders and turning people challenges into practical business solutions, we would like to hear from you.


 


Apply for the HR Business Partner - Momase position and help shape the people capability that supports Islands Petroleum's continued growth and operational performance through this link below. 


 


HR Business Partner - Momase 


 








Apply

28525.description:
Director – Infrastructure & Development Projects 


The Organisation:
 


Pacific Adventist University (PAU) is owned and operated by the South Pacific Division of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. The institution is accredited by the Adventist Accreditation Association, an international denominational authority for all tertiary and graduate educational programs and institutions owned by the Seventh-day Adventist Church entities. The main campus is located on the pristine Koiari Park, 14 miles outside Port Moresby, the capital of Papua New Guinea. The institution was established in 1984. Since then, it has grown from a college of 20 students to a university of over 1000 students from across the Pacific. 


The Role:


The Director – Infrastructure & Development Projects reports to the Bursar/ Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and is responsible for leading the strategic planning, design, and delivery of all infrastructure and capital development initiatives at Pacific Adventist University. This role ensures that the University’s physical environment supports academic excellence, student experience, and long-term institutional sustainability. The role provides leadership in facilities management, project execution, compliance, and stakeholder engagement, ensuring that all development aligns with the University’s mission and values. The Director – Infrastructure & Development Projects leads a dedicated project team and works closely with the Vice Chancellor, Council, and external stakeholders to deliver safe, compliant, and future-focused infrastructure outcomes.


Core Responsibilities:
 




To promote a culture of good governance, transparency and accountability, integrity and service as consistent with the ethos, values and principles of the Seventh-day Adventist Church, and the Vision and Mission of the Pacific Adventist University.


Develop and implement long-term infrastructure strategies aligned with the University’s mission, academic priorities, and community needs.


Provide leadership and oversight for all capital projects, including new construction, major renovations, campus expansion, and infrastructure upgrades. Ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and to quality standards


Provide direction and mentoring to the Projects team, fostering a high-performance culture, collaboration and accountability.


Ensure effective maintenance, refurbishment, and upgrading of existing facilities to meet safety, sustainability, and operational standards.


Guarantee adherence to building codes, occupational health and safety regulations, environmental standards, and University policies.


Prepare and manage budgets for infrastructure projects, ensuring transparency, accountability, and cost control


Collaborate with internal stakeholders, contractors, government agencies, and donors to secure support and ensure project success.


Integrate sustainable design, energy efficiency, and innovative technologies into infrastructure planning and development.


Provide regular reports to the Bursar/CFO, Vice Chancellor and Council on project progress, risks, and outcomes


Under the direction of the Vice-Chancellor to represent the University as required externally in advancing the aspirations and interests of the University.


To serve as Chairperson or as a member of designated University Committees, as well as Ad hoc Committees and Selection Panels as constituted from time to time.


Any other duties as requested by the Bursar/CFO




About you:  


 
 
Qualifications and Skills required: 




A Master’s degree in Engineering, Architecture, Project Management, or related discipline.


Minimum of 10 years’ senior leadership experience in infrastructure development, facilities management, or capital project delivery.


Demonstrated success in managing large-scale projects within higher education, public sector, or corporate environments.


Strong knowledge of building codes, compliance frameworks, and sustainability practices in Papua New Guinea.


Strategic leadership and vision.


Strong project and financial management skills.


Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement abilities.


Commitment to sustainability and innovation.


High ethical standards, integrity, and accountability


Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and manage external contractors effectively


Ability to work in a cross-cultural environment with a commitment to team dynamics and collaborative leadership.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

Core Responsibilities:
 




To promote a culture of good governance, transparency and accountability, integrity and service as consistent with the ethos, values and principles of the Seventh-day Adventist Church, and the Vision and Mission of the Pacific Adventist University.


To provide high-level financial and strategic advice to the Vice-Chancellor and the University Council on all matters pertaining to the fiscal health of the institution.


Oversee the operations of the University’s Finance Office, Farm, Support Services, and Book Shop in counsel with the Vice-Chancellor and in harmony with directives of the University Council and South Pacific Division Policy.


Work with the Vice-Chancellor and other senior administrators of the University in the preparation and implementation of financial reports, annual budget and other operational reports.


Review the monthly financial operation of the University and report to the Vice- Chancellor.


Review annual financial statements for presentation to the University Council.


Maintain an effective reporting system for all the financial operations of the University.


Arrange for the internal auditing of business records and work with the Vice-Chancellor to arrange external auditing by the auditing department of the South Pacific Division.


Serve as custodian of all property and equipment under the administration of the University including the maintenance of safety and security.


Provide for the safekeeping of all funds, securities and other valuables of the University. Investments of funds are to be made in harmony with Division Policy allowing for adequate liquidity.


Make recommendations to the Vice-Chancellor and the University Council on benefits and entitlements for the staff and on charges to students.


Liaise with the Support Services Director regarding the financial aspects of the service and auxiliary business activities of the University and receive periodic reports.


Prepare and present to the Vice-Chancellor and the University Council cost studies of all service and business enterprises of the University.


Maintain regular surveillance of departmental expenditure, ensuring that departmental expenses remain within budget provisions.


Receive from all department’s regular requests for purchase and replacement of equipment and vet or verify these as determined appropriate in terms of budget allowance and/or cost priority.


Be responsible for the maintenance and safe keeping of all financial records including adequate back up of computer-based data.


Foster a campus environment that encourages the spiritual growth of students and staff


Under the direction of the Vice-Chancellor to represent the University as required externally in advancing the aspirations and interests of the University.


To serve as Chairperson or as a member of designated University Committees, as well as Ad hoc Committees and Selection Panels as constituted from time to time.


From time to time the Bursar/CFO maybe requested to act in in the absence of the Vice-Chancellor as necessary and required in ensuring business continuity.


Any other duties as requested by the Vice-Chancellor




 


About you:  


 
Qualifications and Skills required: 




A minimum of a Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or Business Administration; CPA or equivalent professional certification is highly preferred.

Has a strong understanding of higher education systems in Papua New Guinea and the South Pacific, with the capacity to enhance teaching, research, and professional activities.

28522.description:
Admissions & Students Records Officer


 


The Organisation:
 


Pacific Adventist University (PAU) is owned and operated by the South Pacific Division of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. The institution is accredited by the Adventist Accreditation Association, an international denominational authority for all tertiary and graduate educational programs and institutions owned by the Seventh-day Adventist Church entities. The main campus is located on the pristine Koiari Park, 14 miles outside Port Moresby, the capital of Papua New Guinea. The institution was established in 1984. Since then, it has grown from a college of 20 students to a university of over 1,000 students from across the Pacific.


 


The Role:


The Admissions & Student Records Officer reports to the Assistant Registrar and serves as a point of contact for all information relating to Undergraduate and Postgraduate Courses offered by the University. This position is responsible for administering and supporting the student admissions process from application through to the applicant’s acceptance, offer and enrolment. It includes entry requirements, in accordance with institutional admission policies, relevant regulatory requirements and also for information on visa applications for international students.


 


Core Responsibilities:
 




Be responsible for responding to all communication concerning entry requirements, admissions processes and visa applications for international students, from both current and prospective students, as well as parents, sponsors, public and private bodies and other stakeholders.


Be responsible for managing applications electronically (online) or manually (where required) and providing course information or feedback to interested applicants and/or school bodies or nominated representatives.


Review and ensure that completed application forms (online) or manually are ready for screening and selection by the Course Coordinator and/or the School Dean and the Academic Registrar or his/her associate.


Provide administrative support to the student selection process using the Student Management Admissions system.


Manage the application registry accordingly after the screening and selection process is done for each of the applicants for the different admission categories.


Responsible in processing offers and admissions decisions with accompanying documents, ensuring they are conveyed to applicants in a timely manner.


Be responsible for updating and archiving student files aside from any general filing as required within the Academic Office.


Take lead in the preparation and lodgement of entry permit and visa extension application at the PNG Immigration for overseas students and their dependents.


Work with the Academic secretary or designated officer in keeping a register of all students (and dependent) visas and passports kept in the safe, noting their expiry dates monthly and ensure passports and visas are renewed prior to the expiry dates.


Assists with the preparation and release of admissions information as requested with participation in student recruitment and outreach activities such as career expos, open days or other arranged information sessions.


Contribute to an environment of devotion/worship at the Work Team and Department level.


Other duties as directed by the Assistant Registrar.




 


About you:  


Qualifications and Skills required: 




Possesses a PhD or equivalent qualification and is a recognized scholar with expertise relevant to the school’s academic disciplines.


Demonstrates the ability to work effectively in diverse cross-cultural environments while upholding


Active relationship with Jesus Christ, characterized by a deep desire for worship and service to God.


Diploma level qualifications business administration, records/data management, and/or related fields, with a bachelor’s degree to be viewed favourably.


Minimum of 3 years’ experience, preferably in a School Office environment.


A sound working knowledge of, and proven loyalty to, the church its organisation and policies.


Have an interest in and aptitude for cross-cultural ministry.


Knowledge of student admission and enrolment processes.


Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.


Excellent organisational and time management skills.


Proven knowledge of cataloguing and filing.


Proven knowledge of MS applications, with experience in data software highly regarded.


Strong ability to maintain respect and confidentiality of privileged information.


Be knowledgeable of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS).


Be able to take delegation and strong team player.

28663.description:
About Us


New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company committed to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, NPL focuses on the responsible extraction of high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of its employees, the environment, and local communities.
Our dedication to safety, innovation, and ethical mining practices ensure meaningful contributions to the national economy and supports the development and prosperity of the regions in which we operate. At NPL, we aim to create a lasting positive impact by fostering strong stakeholder relationships and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.


About the role


NPL is seeking a detail-oriented and strategic 
Specialist – Sourcing
 to join our Procurement & Supply Chain team based in 
Lae office
. Reporting to the 
Superintendent – Contracts – Supply & Business Services 
the successful candidate will be responsible for identifying sourcing opportunities, evaluating suppliers, negotiating contracts, and maintaining vendor relationships to ensure optimal value for the organization.


About You


To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experience:


•    Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Business Administration, or a related field.
•    Minimum of 3–5 years’ experience in procurement, sourcing, or related roles, preferably within the mining, oil, or gas industries.
•    Strong negotiation and vendor management capabilities.
•    Sound knowledge of procurement legislation, policies, and procedures.
•    Excellent analytical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
•    Proven ability to manage supplier relationships to meet organizational requirements and timelines.
•    Proficiency in drafting scopes of work, evaluation justifications.
•    Experienced in the contract life cycle from planning to contract execution and performance monitoring;
•    Exposure and experienced in Contractor Management.
•    Strong computer literacy, including experience with integrated management systems, word processing, and spreadsheet software.
•    Familiarity with procurement processes and documentation requirements.
•    Competency in using procurement modules within systems such as SAP.
•    Effective negotiation and influencing skills across diverse teams and stakeholders.
•    General understanding of supply chain processes including inventory management, warehousing, and logistics (desirable).
•    Knowledge of invoice discrepancy processes (desirable).
•    Ability to multitask and prioritize effectively.
•    Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with the NPL’s Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health and safety rules and procedures


Key Responsibilities:


•    Manage the end-to-end sourcing and contract lifecycle. 
•    Develop and implement sourcing strategies. 
•    Collaborate with user departments to develop scopes or specifications. 
•    Conduct competitive bidding processes (e.g., Request for Proposals). 
•    Prepare procurement plans, tender documentation, and manage the tender process. 
•    Coordinate supplier evaluation meetings and facilitate approvals. 
•    Lead supplier negotiations and discussions. 
•    Draft and finalize contracts for approval and execution. 
•    Ensure compliance with corporate policy requirements. 
•    Monitor supplier performance and contract compliance. 
•    Analyze proposals, pricing, and financial data for price reasonableness. 
•    Manage contract price reviews and update pricing in SAP. 
•    Build and maintain a network of potential suppliers. 
•    Lead cost analysis and improvement initiatives. 
•    Support purchasing, inventory, and logistics teams as needed. 
•    Liaise with end users, legal advisors, and other departments to deliver value-added services. 
•    Manage onboarding requirements for new suppliers. 
•    Consolidate supplier and contractor base. 
•    Ensure sourcing and purchasing activities align with corporate supply chain policies and procedures. 
•    A Monthly travel to Porgera Mine Site will also be arrange when required while residing in Lae.


Mobilization Requirement


This is a PNG National Staff position based in Lae-based office, operating on five (5) days on and two (2) days off and/or ten (10) days on and four (4) days off rotation.


Applicants must reside in 
Lae 
and will be required to:


•    Successfully complete a pre-employment medical examination, including drug and alcohol screening (arranged for shortlisted candidates’ post-interview).
•    Provide a valid Police Clearance Certificate issued within the last six (6) months.


 
           Closing Date: Sunday 04th October 2026






Apply

We are seeking a reliable and responsible 
Admin Driver
 to join our Finance and Administration Department, based at our Lae Head Office.


 


The primary responsibility of this position is to safely transport staff, materials, and documents while ensuring company vehicles are properly maintained and operated.


 


Duties and Responsibilities 




Safely drive company vehicles to transport staff, clients, materials, and documents


Maintain accurate, vehicle-specific fuel consumption records.


Ensure company vehicles are always kept clean and presentable.


Conduct basic checks of vehicles and report any faults, defects, or maintenance requirements immediately.


Ensure vehicles are operated in accordance with company policies and road safety requirements.


Demonstrate reliability, punctuality, and a strong sense of responsibility.


Assist with basic office and administrative duties as required.

Grade 10 or 12 certificate.


Minimum three (3) years’ driving experience with Valid Class 6 Licence


Good knowledge of Lae roads and surrounding areas.


Strong commitment to road safety and adherence to traffic rules.


Physically fit and of sober habits.


Reliable, punctual, and trustworthy and with good communication and interpersonal skills.

28674.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.


Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.


About the role


Reporting to the Operations Supervisor, this role is responsible for ensuring the safe and efficient delivery of drilling pads to support the Company’s exploration drilling programs.


Key / Major Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.


• Operate and maintain mini excavators and skid steer loaders in accordance with K92 Plant Operations & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.
• Conduct pre-start inspections and basic troubleshooting on equipment to identify and address potential issues.
• Construct drill pads, helipads, and access walkways in a mountainous exploration environment.
• Monitor the condition of work pads and surrounding areas, ensuring ongoing safety and stability.


About
 You


To be considered for this role, you must have a class Four [4] Driver's License that allows f Excavator on public roads, and you must also have experience in operating excavator smaller than 20T. You must also have:




commitment to safety [essential]


knowledge of small excavator


ability to work autonomously independently with limited supervision


General knowledge of mobile equipment




Life at K92  


Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

28647.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


In this role you will play an important role in ensuring the mine remains operational by making sure that the underground roads are well maintained and that the haul trucks can operate in an efficient manner.


Key / Major Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.




Maintaining underground roadways to ensure safety and functionality.


Completing pre-start inspections and reporting mechanical issues or damage.


Upholding strict safety standards and supporting a positive workplace culture.


Collaborating with supervisors and the team to meet operational priorities.




About You


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you are physically strong and healthy and have minimum Grade 10 level of education. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.




Physically fit - able to pass a pre-employment medical


Have a minimum of a grade 10 educational qualification


Be able to read and write Pidgin and English,


Ability to work with people from different ethnic groups.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

28577.description:
We hiring 
Marketing Manager – Pactrade (PNG) Limited


PacTrade PNG Ltd is a leading distributor of Fiji-manufactured and renowned international Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) in Papua New Guinea. The Company represents a diverse portfolio of established consumer brands and services an extensive customer network across major supermarkets, wholesalers, food service customers and down-the-line (DTL) retailers. As part Of the wider CJ Patel Group, the business is focused on strengthening its market presence in Papua New Guinea through effective brand management, customer partnerships, distribution excellence and consumer-focused marketing initiatives.


THE ROLE


We are seeking a dynamic, commercially focused and experienced Marketing Manager to lead the marketing and brand activations function for PacTrade PNG Ltd. The Marketing Manager will be responsible for developing and implementing short- and long-term marketing strategies for the Company's portfolio of CJ Patel Brands and represented international brands. Working closely with the Sales Team, Marketing Coordinators, regional stakeholders and brand principals, the position will drive brand growth, consumer awareness, market penetration and effective execution of marketing initiatives across PNG.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




Develop and implement annual marketing and brand plans aligned with the Company's growth objectives.


Lead marketing strategies for local and international FMCG brands.Plan and execute product launches, promotions and activations across key retail and outstation markets.


Drive trade marketing and in-store execution, including hands-on involvement in brand activations at retail and Outstation markets.


Manage digital and social media marketing initiatives.


Analyse market performance and identify growth opportunities.


Lead and support Marketing Coordinators.


Manage marketing budget and ensure compliance with brand guidelines


Identify new marketing opportunities and channels




QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE




A Bachelor's Degree in Marketing, Business, Commerce, Management or a related discipline


At least 5 years' relevant marketing experience in FMCG, retail or distribution, with brand management experience


Proven experience in planning and executing brand activations, trade marketing campaigns and consumer promotions.


Previous leadership or supervisory experience will be highly regarded.


Strong understanding of FMCG brand management, trade marketing consumer prornotions and route-to-rnarket environments


Sound digital and social media marketing knowledge.


Strong commercial and analytical capability to interpret sales, market and campaign performance data


Experience managing markefng budgets, agencies and external service providers
